source.name: AirStack category guides
source.note: Written by AirStack to explain what each category is for and who uses it. Not a vendor claim and not a measurement.

meta.what: Meta's apps, AI models and open-source developer projects, grouped by maker so you can see them in one place.
why: Open-source libraries and models your team can run and change itself
Consumer apps where your customers and audience already are
One maker's AI, apps and code in one view, next to the alternatives
jobs: Train or fine-tune a machine learning model
Write a web or mobile app interface
Run an open model on your own hardware
Post and reply to your audience
meta.watch_for: Open model licences can carry their own use terms; read each licence before you ship a product on it.

creative-ai.what: Generates images, video, voice and music from a text prompt or a reference, so you can draft visual and audio work quickly.
why: Make ad, social and product visuals without a full shoot
Draft storyboards and concepts before you commit a budget
Turn a script into a narrated or presenter-led video
Try many versions of one idea quickly
jobs: Generate a product or ad image
Turn a script into a short video
Create a voiceover or soundtrack
Remove a background or upscale an image
creative-ai.watch_for: Generation is usually metered in credits, and usage rights for outputs differ by plan; check both before you publish.

email-calendar.what: Your inbox, your calendar and the booking links people use to find a time with you.
why: Fewer back-and-forth emails to find a meeting time
Shared calendars so teams see who is free
Faster sorting of a busy inbox
Booking pages that let customers pick a slot themselves
jobs: Send, sort and file email
Book a meeting from a shared link
See a colleague's free time
Block focus time on your calendar
email-calendar.watch_for: Add-on scheduling and inbox tools often overlap with your email suite; check what your current plan already includes.

docs-storage.what: Stores and shares files, and lets people write, edit and comment on documents together in one place.
why: One current version of each document instead of attachments
Access from any device, with sharing you can revoke
A searchable home for team knowledge and how-to pages
Version history when something is deleted or overwritten
jobs: Write and comment on a shared document
Share a file with someone outside your company
Publish a team wiki or handbook
Restore an earlier version of a file
Sign or mark up a PDF
docs-storage.watch_for: Storage caps and per-user pricing add up as you grow, and moving folders and permissions to another tool is hard.

chat-meetings.what: Team messaging, voice and video calls in one place, so people can talk in real time or catch up later.
why: Fewer internal emails, with questions answered in channels
Video calls with screen sharing for remote teams
A searchable history of decisions and discussions
Business phone lines and call routing for sales or support
jobs: Message a team or project channel
Start a video call and share your screen
Record a short video walkthrough
Route customer calls to the right person
Search past discussions
chat-meetings.watch_for: Free tiers often limit message history or call length; check retention and guest access before your team depends on it.

project-management.what: Tracks who is doing what by when: tasks, projects and timelines the whole team can see and update.
why: Priorities, owners and due dates in one place
Fewer status meetings, because progress shows on the board
Spot blocked or late work before it slips further
Plan sprints, launches or client work against capacity
jobs: Assign a task with an owner and due date
Plan a sprint or release
Track a project on a board or timeline
Report progress to stakeholders
Log and triage bugs
project-management.watch_for: Per-user pricing often counts everyone who edits, not just managers; check how guests and viewers are billed.

design.what: Creates and reviews visual work: interfaces, graphics, diagrams, whiteboards and presentations, often with others live.
why: Designers and reviewers comment on the same file
Shared components make products and brand consistent
Non-designers make on-brand graphics from templates
Whiteboards for workshops and planning with remote teams
jobs: Design a screen or clickable prototype
Hand off specs to developers
Make a social graphic from a template
Run a remote whiteboard workshop
Draw a diagram or flowchart
design.watch_for: Editor licences are often billed separately from viewers; check who needs edit rights and how files export if you switch.

ai-assistants.what: Chat-based AI that drafts, summarises, translates and answers questions, and can search your files when you allow it.
why: Faster first drafts of emails, documents and reports
Answers from your own company files, not just the web
Quick translation and rewriting for tone or clarity
Research summaries with links you can check
jobs: Draft or rewrite a document
Summarise a long file or thread
Translate text for a customer
Search across company knowledge
Answer a question with cited sources
ai-assistants.watch_for: Check whether your data is used for training, where it is stored, and whether the plan meets your privacy rules.

ai-coding.what: Editors and assistants that suggest, write, explain and review code inside the tools developers already use.
why: Less time on boilerplate, tests and repetitive edits
Faster onboarding to an unfamiliar codebase
An automated first-pass review on every pull request
Answers about your code without leaving the editor
jobs: Complete code as you type
Explain or refactor a file
Write unit tests for a function
Review a pull request
Find and fix a bug
ai-coding.watch_for: Limits on premium models can lead to usage-based overages; check the monthly allowance and how your code is handled.

crm-sales.what: Records every customer, deal and conversation so a sales team can see its pipeline and follow up on time.
why: One record of each customer and deal, not scattered sheets
Forecasts based on pipeline stages, not guesses
Reminders so follow-ups are not missed
Call and email history the next rep can pick up
jobs: Log a call or meeting with a prospect
Move a deal through pipeline stages
Make a list of target accounts
Send a sequence of follow-up emails
Forecast the quarter's revenue
crm-sales.watch_for: Contracts are often annual with a minimum number of users, and automation or data features may sit in add-ons.

marketing.what: Runs campaigns: email and social posts, search and website analytics, and the lists and audiences you send them to.
why: Automated emails that reach people at the right moment
Schedule social posts across channels from one place
See which keywords and pages bring in visitors
Learn which campaigns lead to sign-ups and sales
jobs: Send a newsletter or email campaign
Schedule a week of social posts
Research keywords for a blog post
Set up a welcome email sequence
See where visitors click on a page
marketing.watch_for: Email tools often price by contact count, so costs rise as your list grows; remove inactive contacts and check overage terms.

support.what: Collects customer questions from email, chat and social into one queue so a team can answer, track and learn from them.
why: No customer message lost between inboxes
Faster answers with saved replies and a help centre
Self-service articles that answer common questions
Reports on response times and recurring problems
jobs: Answer and assign a customer ticket
Run live chat on your website
Publish help centre articles
Escalate a bug to engineering
Track customer satisfaction
support.watch_for: AI reply features are often billed by usage on top of per-agent pricing; check how each conversation is counted.

hr-people.what: Runs the employee lifecycle: hiring, onboarding, payroll, benefits, time off, reviews and records in one system.
why: Payroll and tax filings handled on schedule
One place for candidates, interviews and offers
Employees update their own details and request leave
Hire, pay and onboard people in other countries
jobs: Run payroll
Post a job and track candidates
Onboard a new hire
Approve a time-off request
Run a performance review cycle
hr-people.watch_for: Pricing is usually per employee per month, and payroll, benefits and recruiting are often separate modules.

finance.what: Records money in and out: bookkeeping, invoices, payments, cards and expenses, so the books are right at month end.
why: A faster month-end close with bank feeds and matching
Get paid sooner with online invoices and payments
Company cards and expense rules that cut receipt chasing
Accurate numbers for tax, investors and lenders
jobs: Reconcile bank transactions
Send an invoice and take payment
Approve and pay a supplier bill
Submit an expense with a receipt
Close the books for the month
finance.watch_for: Payment tools take a share of each transaction, and moving ledger history later is hard; check fees and exports early.

security-it.what: Protects accounts, devices and data: passwords, sign-in, device management, threat detection and compliance evidence.
why: One sign-in for every app, removed the day someone leaves
Shared passwords stored safely, not in spreadsheets
Laptops set up, encrypted and patched remotely
Evidence ready when customers ask about your security
jobs: Set up single sign-on for an app
Share a password with a team
Enrol and lock a company laptop
Collect evidence for a security audit
Respond to a security alert
security-it.watch_for: Single sign-on and audit logs often sit on higher tiers; check which plan includes them before you roll out.

data-bi.what: Collects, stores and charts your data so people can answer questions about customers, product use and the business.
why: Dashboards everyone trusts instead of conflicting spreadsheets
See how people use your product and where they drop off
Move data from your apps into one warehouse
Answer new questions without asking an engineer each time
jobs: Make a dashboard for weekly metrics
Track sign-ups and drop-off in a funnel
Sync app data into a warehouse
Run an ad hoc query
Share a report with leadership
data-bi.watch_for: Many tools bill by events, rows or compute used, so costs can jump as traffic grows; set alerts and limits early.

dev-platforms.what: Where software is stored, tested, deployed and run: code hosting, cloud hosting, APIs, monitoring and on-call.
why: Review and merge code changes safely as a team
Deploy automatically on every change
Hear about errors and outages before customers report them
Run apps and databases without managing servers
jobs: Host code and review pull requests
Deploy a web app
Monitor errors and performance
Page the on-call engineer
Test an API
dev-platforms.watch_for: Usage-based billing for compute, bandwidth and logs can spike without warning; set budgets and alerts before launch.

web-commerce.what: Creates and runs your website or online store: pages, hosting, domains, content, checkout and orders.
why: A professional site without hiring a developer
Take payments and manage orders online
Update pages and blog posts without code
Hosting, security updates and domains handled for you
jobs: Launch a website from a template
Add products and take online payments
Publish a blog post
Connect a custom domain
Manage content for several sites
web-commerce.watch_for: Transaction fees, paid apps and themes add to the plan price, and moving a store to another platform takes real work.

legal-contracts.what: Drafts, sends, signs and tracks contracts, and for law firms runs matters, billing and client records.
why: Contracts signed online, without printing or scanning
Every signed agreement findable in one place
Renewal and notice dates that do not slip by
Approved templates so sales can send terms without waiting
jobs: Send a contract for e-signature
Draft from an approved template
Track renewal and notice dates
Review a contract against your playbook
Log time and bill a client matter
legal-contracts.watch_for: E-signature plans often cap how many documents you can send; check the limit and what each extra send costs.

forms-surveys.what: Collects answers from people: forms, quizzes, surveys and feedback, with results in a sheet or report.
why: One structured form instead of email back-and-forth
Measure customer or employee satisfaction over time
Send answers straight into your other tools
Branded forms that show only the questions that apply
jobs: Create a sign-up or order form
Send a customer feedback survey
Run an employee engagement survey
Send responses into a spreadsheet or CRM
Collect payments or file uploads
forms-surveys.watch_for: Response limits and branding removal are often on paid tiers; check the limits and who owns the response data.

spend-procurement.what: Controls company spending before it happens: purchase requests, approvals, supplier contracts, travel and renewals.
why: Every purchase approved by the right person first
See software and supplier contracts before they renew
Book travel within policy without manual checks
Fewer duplicate tools and surprise renewals
jobs: Request and approve a purchase
Onboard a new supplier
Book a business trip within policy
Track contract renewal dates
Negotiate a software renewal
spend-procurement.watch_for: A new approval step slows purchasing if it is not connected to your accounting system and cards; check both links.

learning.what: Delivers and tracks training: course libraries, compliance courses, onboarding paths and tools to create your own lessons.
why: Assign required compliance training and prove it was done
Onboard new hires with the same material every time
Give staff a library of courses for new skills
Sell or share your own courses with customers
jobs: Assign a course to a team
Track completion of required training
Create a course from your own material
Run a customer education programme
Report on skills by team
learning.watch_for: Course libraries are often priced per learner whether used or not; check activity reports and content exports.

video-webinars.what: Hosts, records and streams video: webinars, virtual events, live streams and video libraries you can embed and share.
why: Reach a large audience without a venue
Collect registrations and follow up with attendees
Record once and replay on demand
Host video on your own site without ads
jobs: Run a webinar with registration
Stream live to several platforms at once
Record a podcast or interview remotely
Host and embed a product video
Send replays to registrants
video-webinars.watch_for: Plans are often capped by attendee count or hosting hours; check what happens when an event goes over the limit.

it-service.what: Takes requests and incidents from employees, tracks devices and software, and lets IT fix problems remotely.
why: Every IT request logged, assigned and tracked to done
Self-service answers for common requests like resets
Remote access to fix a laptop without a desk visit
A current list of devices, licences and owners
jobs: Log and resolve an employee ticket
Reset access or a password
Patch and update company laptops
Connect remotely to a user's computer
Track hardware and software assets
it-service.watch_for: Remote-access and device tools may price per technician and per device; count both before you compare plans.

coding-agents.what: AI agents that take a coding task, read your repository, edit files and run commands until the task is done.
why: Hand off well-defined changes and review the result
Run fixes, upgrades and tests from the terminal
Work through a backlog of small tasks in parallel
Choose or swap the model behind the agent
jobs: Implement a small feature from an issue
Fix a failing test
Upgrade a dependency across a repository
Explain how a codebase fits together
Open a pull request for review
coding-agents.watch_for: Agents run commands on your machine and use model credits fast; set permissions and spend limits before you hand off work.

llm-sdks-and-routers.what: Code libraries and gateways for calling language models from your app, often across several providers through one interface.
why: Switch or combine model providers without rewriting code
Fall back to another model when one is down or slow
Track usage and cost per team, app or customer
Streaming, retries and structured output handled for you
jobs: Call a model from your application
Route requests across several providers
Stream responses to a chat interface
Set rate limits and budgets per key
Get structured data back from a model
llm-sdks-and-routers.watch_for: A layer between you and the provider can lag new model features; check how quickly it supports the options you rely on.

vector-dbs.what: Stores text, images and other data as embeddings so your app can find items by meaning, not just keywords.
why: Let an AI assistant answer from your own documents
Search that finds results by meaning, not exact words
Recommend similar products, articles or tickets
Filter by metadata and permissions alongside similarity
jobs: Index documents for retrieval
Run a semantic search query
Find similar items for recommendations
Filter results by user permissions
Update embeddings when content changes
vector-dbs.watch_for: Cost and speed depend on data size and query volume; test with your real data, and check how hard it is to export.

llm-observability.what: Records each prompt, response, tool call and cost in your AI app so you can trace, debug and improve it.
why: See why an AI answer went wrong
Track cost and latency per feature or customer
Catch quality drops after a model or prompt change
Turn real conversations into test cases
jobs: Trace a multi-step agent run
Compare two prompt versions
Monitor cost and latency
Flag bad answers for review
Export traces into an eval dataset
llm-observability.watch_for: Traces can hold customer data and grow fast; check retention, redaction and per-trace pricing before you log everything.

meeting-notes.what: Records, transcribes and summarises meetings, then shares notes and action items with the people who need them.
why: Stay in the conversation instead of typing notes
A searchable record of what was decided and by whom
Action items sent to your CRM or task tool
Catch up on a missed meeting without the recording
jobs: Record and transcribe a call
Share a summary with attendees
Search past meetings for a decision
Send action items to a task tool
Log sales call notes in the CRM
meeting-notes.watch_for: Your meeting suite may already take notes; check its languages, in-person support and recording consent rules first.

agent-frameworks.what: Code libraries for AI agents that plan steps, call tools, remember context and hand work to other agents.
why: Ready-made parts for tool calls, memory and retries
Multi-step tasks structured so they are easier to debug
Several specialised agents working on one job
Less tie-in to a single model provider
jobs: Give a model tools to call
Chain steps into a workflow
Add memory across a conversation
Hand off between specialised agents
Pause for human approval
agent-frameworks.watch_for: Frameworks change quickly and add layers to debug; prefer the smallest one that does the job, and pin versions.

llm-evals.what: Tests the quality of AI outputs against datasets and rules, so you know if a change made answers better or worse.
why: Catch regressions before a prompt or model change ships
Compare models on your own tasks, not public benchmarks
Score answers for accuracy, safety and format
A shared quality bar for product and engineering
jobs: Run a test set against a new prompt
Compare two models on your own data
Check answers for made-up facts
Red-team for unsafe outputs
Add evals to continuous integration
llm-evals.watch_for: A model grading another model can be wrong too; check a sample of scores by hand before you trust them.

local-inference.what: Runs language models on your own laptop or servers instead of sending data to a hosted provider.
why: Data stays on machines you control
Work offline or in restricted networks
No per-request charges once you own the hardware
Try open models before you commit to one
jobs: Run an open model on a laptop
Serve a model behind an internal API
Test a model before deploying it
Run models in an air-gapped network
Quantise a model to fit your hardware
local-inference.watch_for: Smaller local models may not match hosted quality, and serving many users needs real GPUs; test on your own tasks first.

speech-ai.what: Turns speech into text and text into natural-sounding speech, and runs voice agents that talk with people live.
why: Transcribe calls, videos and podcasts automatically
Add voice to apps, games or accessibility features
Answer phone calls with a voice agent
Subtitles and captions in many languages
jobs: Transcribe an audio or video file
Caption a video
Generate a voiceover from text
Run a live voice agent on calls
Identify who spoke when
speech-ai.watch_for: Accuracy varies by accent, noise and language; test with your own recordings, and check consent rules for cloned voices.

browser-agents.what: Lets AI agents open web pages, click, type and extract content, so they can do tasks on sites that have no API.
why: Automate web tasks on sites that offer no API
Turn web pages into clean text for AI models
Let a coding agent test your app in a real browser
Run many browser sessions in the cloud
jobs: Fill in a web form automatically
Scrape a page into structured data
Test a web app end to end
Log in and download a report
Crawl a site for AI retrieval
browser-agents.watch_for: Sites change layouts and block bots; check each site's terms, expect breakage, and avoid giving agents your own passwords.

ai-app-builders.what: Turns a plain-English description into a working web or mobile app that you can edit, host and publish.
why: A working prototype in front of users quickly
Non-engineers can make internal tools themselves
Test an idea before hiring a development team
Hosting, database and sign-in set up for you
jobs: Prototype an app from a prompt
Make an internal tool or dashboard
Add sign-in and a database
Publish to a custom domain
Export the code to a repository
ai-app-builders.watch_for: Each prompt uses credits, and apps can be hard to move off the platform; check limits and code export before you rely on one.

workflow-automation.what: Connects your apps so an event in one, like a new form entry or email, triggers actions in others without manual work.
why: Stop copying data between apps by hand
Fewer missed steps in routine processes
Add AI steps to processes you already run
Ops teams automate without waiting on engineers
jobs: Send new leads from a form to your CRM
Post alerts to a chat channel
Sync records between two apps
Run a scheduled report
Add an AI step to summarise or classify
workflow-automation.watch_for: Pricing often counts every task or step run, so busy workflows can cost more than expected; estimate your volume first.
